chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from al-Husayn ibn Hashim, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, and he looked at a beautiful boy: 'It is fitting that the father of this boy would have eaten the quince.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the father eating quince in relation to the boy's beauty in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical beauty of a boy to his father's consumption of quince (*safarjal*), reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of *tathir* (purification) and how parental diet influences the constitution of offspring. This narrative is often cited in discussions on *tadbir al-nikah* (marital management) and the spiritual-physical preparation of parents, emphasizing that nourishment affects not just health but also aesthetic and temperamental traits. It underscores the holistic view in Shia tradition where physical habits are intertwined with spiritual and hereditary outcomes.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymuli, from Al Husayn Bin Hashim, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said and looked at a beautiful boy: ‘It is a must that the father of this boy would have eaten the quince’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Taymuliy, from al-Husayn ibn Hashim from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, while looking at a beautiful boy said, ‘It seems the father of this boy had been eating quince.’”
